    Rank bounds for a pencil of linear maps #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.finrank_range_baseChange {k : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} {U : Type u_3} {V : Type u_4} [Field k] [Field F] [Algebra k F] [AddCommGroup U] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k U] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k U] [Module.Finite k V] (A : U →ₗ[k] V) :
    Module.finrank F ↥(LinearMap.baseChange F A).range = Module.finrank k ↥A.range

    Extension of scalars preserves the rank of a linear map over a field.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.affine_finrank_range_eval_le {k : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} {U : Type u_3} {V : Type u_4} [Field k] [Field F] [Algebra k F] [AddCommGroup U] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k U] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k U] [Module.Finite k V] (e : Polynomial k →ₐ[k] F) (he : Function.Injective ⇑e) (A B : U →ₗ[k] V) (t : k) :
    Module.finrank k ↥(A + t • B).range ≤ Module.finrank F ↥(LinearMap.baseChange F A + e Polynomial.X • LinearMap.baseChange F B).range

    The rank of a pencil at any ground-field parameter is at most its rank where the parameter is transcendental.
